title: Stabilize kernel probing under capacity surges via probe-dampening and rate-aware backoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description: After the 2026-02-20 high-utilization event a subset of inference workers began rapidly switching execution kernels in response to speculative probe results. This produced oscillatory behavior that amplified tail latencies (p95/p99) for models with mixed quantization and long KV-cache warmups. The regression surfaced in hosted clusters and affected several enterprise customers on Dedicated with bursty traffic patterns.
timeline_summary: 2026-02-20 detection by SRE alerting; initial rollback of speculative probe increase same day; 2026-02-22 hotfix to reduce global probe frequency; 2026-02-24 exploratory bench produced repro; 2026-02-26 ticket created to own followups and durable fixes; 2026-03-02 canary rollout of dampening heuristics started; 2026-03-10 tests passing and drafting rollout playbook.
impact_details: Observed p95 increase from 120ms to 420ms and p99 spikes to >1.2s on affected requests. Throughput per GPU decreased ~12% under identical load due to repeated kernel swaps and KV cache invalidation overhead. Customers reported intermittent 5xx due to request timeouts when tail latency exceeded route SLOs.
root_cause: Aggressive speculative kernel probing heuristics introduced in scheduler change (PR #3421) increased probe frequency during transient capacity fluctuations. Probes were unbounded per-worker and did not account for recent probe outcomes or per-slot lease contention, causing repeated kernel reloads and KV cache thrash.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Rollback speculative probe rate increase (completed 2026-02-20). 2) Emergency rate-cap per worker (hotfix) to limit probes to 1 per 6s per worker (deployed 2026-02-22). 3) Canary fallback to last-known-good kernel for repeat probe failures (deployed to 10% of capacity on 2026-03-02).
long_term_plan_summary: Implement probe-dampening state machine with exponential backoff, add scheduler-wide probe budget (burst-aware lease), instrument new metrics and synthetic benchmarks, and introduce an acceptance test in CI to detect probe thrash regressions before rollout.
detailed_action_items: AI-1: Implement per-worker exponential probe backoff and a 3-stage dampening state machine (Owner: Liam O'Connor, ETA: 2026-03-12, Estimate: 3)
AI-2: Add global probe budget per scheduler shard and burst-aware lease to prevent synchronized probing across workers (Owner: Mei Chen, ETA: 2026-03-16, Estimate: 5)

AI-3: Create synthetic workload generator that reproduces KV-warmup + bursty arrival patterns; add nightly regression job and alert on probe_rate_per_worker > threshold (Owner: Carlos Reyes, ETA: 2026-03-09, Estimate: 2)

AI-4: Add canary gating rules to console rollout UI to automatically restrict probe-related flags to limited percentage and abort if p95 increases >25% during canary (Owner: Priya Singh, ETA: 2026-03-15, Estimate: 2)

AI-5: Update observability dashboards with new metrics: probe_rate_per_worker, probe_failure_ratio, kv_cache_warmup_ms, kernel_reload_count and create an alert runbook (Owner: SRE Team, ETA: 2026-03-12, Estimate: 3)

AI-6: Postmortem document and customer communication template to notify impacted Dedicated customers and include compensation options if SLA breached (Owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2026-03-14, Estimate: 1)
acceptance_criteria: 1) CI regression detects any increase in probe_rate_per_worker beyond baseline and fails the build. 2) Canary rollout of dampening shows p95 within 10% of baseline on two independent clusters and no p99 regressions. 3) Dashboard and alerts are live and documented in runbook.
testing_plan: Unit tests for backoff state transitions; integration test with synthetic generator validating stabilized kernel choices under 1000 concurrent simulated users; canary on two clusters with telemetry monitoring for 48h; rollback criteria defined in canary gating.

retro_summary: Root cause: unbounded speculative probes + lack of probe budget/gating. The team responded quickly with rollback and hotfix, but followups required to avoid re-introducing unsafe heuristics. Key learnings: always pair speculative optimizations with circuit-breakers and observability, add synthetic regressions for complex scheduling heuristics, and gate runtime flags behind canary automation.
next_steps: Complete AI-1 and AI-2, finish dashboards and alerts, run 48h canary on two clusters, update PRD to include probe budget requirement for future scheduler changes.
